title: Staggered-density canary schedule and quality-signature for graduated rollouts
creator: Asha Bhat
description: Purpose: Define and validate a staggered-density canary pattern that exercises the service across realistic traffic densities and surface a concise quality signature for automated go/no-go gates. Rationale: traditional fixed-fraction canaries miss density-dependent regressions (e.g., KV cache pressure, batching edge cases, kernel scheduling thresholds). This ticket designs a schedule that cycles through low, medium, and high request density with short stress pulses and collects a compact evaluation signature to drive rollout gates and automatic rollback rules.
milestones: 1) Design & metrics spec complete by 2026-03-10; 2) Instrumentation and dashboards in place by 2026-03-24; 3) Dry-run against synthetic workloads 2026-03-30; 4) First customer-facing canary (0.5% traffic) 2026-04-02; 5) Graduated rollout to 10% with automated gate checks by 2026-04-09.
rollout_schedule: Phase A: density sweep (0.1% burst -> 0.5% steady -> 1.5% short pulse) over 48h. Phase B: repeat sweep with regional variation for 72h. Phase C: expand to 5% / 10% once signature passes for two consecutive windows. Each phase includes a hold window for manual review and automated checks.
metrics: Primary: tail latency (p50/p95/p99), error rate, token-cost delta, upstream retries, KV cache hit ratio. Secondary: CPU/GPU utilization, batch size distribution, memory pressure, cold-start rate. Signature: compact vector formed from normalized deltas of p99, error rate, and cache hit ratio compared to baseline.
acceptance_criteria: 1) Signature deviation threshold defined and validated on synthetic runs. 2) Dashboards show stable baselines and automated alerts configured. 3) Playbook steps allow a human in the loop with one-click rollback. 4) No high-severity customer incidents in 72h following 10% expansion.
risks: Risk: false positives from noisy baselines may block safe rollouts. Mitigation: require two consecutive passing windows and use outlier detection smoothing. Risk: instrumentation cost and increased billing on short stress pulses. Mitigation: limit pulse duration and run synthetic runs in dedicated test capacity.
decisions: 1) Use normalized p99 + error-rate + cache-hit vector as the canonical signature. 2) Require two consecutive 30-minute windows of passing checks before expansion. 3) Integrate with existing rollout automation for automatic rollback at 3x baseline error-rate or p99 regression > 2x baseline.
next_steps: Finalize thresholds with SRE and ML infra, land instrumentation PRs, schedule synthetic dry-run and invite Eng/QA/SEs for a war-room during the first customer-facing canary.
